questions.problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x+y\le 2,\,1\le x-y\le 2,\,1\le z\le (x-y)(x+y)\}.
$$

By performing the change of variables

$$
u=x+y,\,v=x-y,\,w=\sqrt{z},
$$

the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}3\sqrt{z}\,dV
$$

can be written in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w$ as
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x+y,\,v=x-y,\,w=\sqrt{z}
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,1\le v\le 2,\,1\le {w}^{2}\le uv\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2\sqrt{z}}\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{z}}(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{z}}(-1-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{w}\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=-w.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}3\sqrt{z}\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}3w\cdot |-w|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}3{w}^{2}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{uv}3{w}^{2}\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le \frac{2x-y}{2}\le 1,\,0\le \frac{y}{2}\le 2,\,0\le z\le 3\}.
$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{2x-y}{2},\,v=\frac{y}{2},\,w=\frac{z}{3},
$$

which of the following could be the missing part of the expression below?

$$
{∭}_{R}(\frac{2x-y}{2}+\frac{z}{3})\,dV={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{2x-y}{2},\,v=\frac{y}{2},\,w=\frac{z}{3},
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2,\,0\le w\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,\,\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{3}|\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & \,\,\,\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=6.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(\frac{2x-y}{2}+\frac{z}{3})\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}(u+w)\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}(u+w)\cdot |6|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,6(u+w)\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=x+y,\,v=y-x,\,w=z,
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
∭(x+y){e}^{y-x}\,dV,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x+y\le 2,\,0\le y-x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 3\}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x+y,\,v=y-x,\,w=z,
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 1,\,0\le w\le 3\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1-(-1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(x+y){e}^{y-x}\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}u{e}^{v}\cdot |-\frac{1}{2}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{u{e}^{v}}{2}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{u{e}^{v}}{2}\,dw\,dv\,du \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}u\,du\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{v}\,dv\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}dw \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot [\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}]_{u=1}^{u=2}\cdot {[{e}^{v}]}_{v=0}^{v=1}\cdot [w]_{w=0}^{w=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2-\frac{1}{2})\cdot (e-1)\cdot (3-0) \\  & =\frac{9}{4}(e-1)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le {x}^{2}-y\le 1,\,1\le \,x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 3\}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
-1\le {x}^{2}-y\le 1,\,1\le \,x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 3,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u={x}^{2}-y,\,v=x,\,w=z.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,1\le v\le 2,\,0\le w\le 3\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2x & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=1.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}dV & ={∭}_{Δ}1\cdot |1|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\,dw\,dv\,du \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}du\cdot {\int }_{1}^{2}dv\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}dw \\  & =[u]_{u=-1}^{u=1}\cdot [v]_{v=1}^{v=2}\cdot [w]_{w=0}^{w=3} \\  & =(1-(-1))\cdot (2-1)\cdot (3-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y-{e}^{x}\le 1,\,1\le y\le 2,\,0\le z{e}^{-x}\le 1\}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
0\le y-{e}^{x}\le 1,\,1\le y\le 2,\,0\le z{e}^{-x}\le 1,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=y-{e}^{x},\,v=y,\,w=z{e}^{-x}.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,1\le v\le 2,\,0\le w\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-{e}^{x} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -z{e}^{-x} & 0 & {e}^{-x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-{e}^{x} & 0 \\ -z{e}^{-x} & {e}^{-x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=-1.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}dV & ={∭}_{Δ}1\cdot |-1|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}dw\,dv\,du \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}du\cdot {\int }_{1}^{2}dv\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}dw \\  & =[u]_{u=0}^{u=1}\cdot [v]_{v=1}^{v=2}\cdot [w]_{w=0}^{w=1} \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2-1)\cdot (1-0) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
